proposed.text: According to Trap #21, where does a wheelchair user make their turning maneuver when using an accessible elevator — inside the car or in the lobby?

options.text: Inside the car — the 1200 × 1400 mm car provides sufficient space for a standard wheelchair turning radius
In the elevator lobby — the 1800 × 1800 mm lobby provides the turning space the small car cannot
Inside the car for standard wheelchairs; in the lobby only for power wheelchairs and scooters
Either location is acceptable as long as the combined car-plus-lobby area equals 1800 × 1800 mm

rationale.summary: Trap #21: the wheelchair turn happens in the lobby (1800 × 1800 mm), not inside the car.
rationale.explanation: Trap #21 in the article. The standard accessible elevator car is 1200 mm wide × 1400 mm deep — not large enough for a wheelchair to make a full 180° turning maneuver (which requires ~1800 mm diameter). BP 344 requires the elevator lobby to provide 1800 × 1800 mm clear turning space. The user approaches in the lobby, turns if needed, then enters the car forward or backs in. The lobby, not the car, is the functional turning zone.
common_misconceptions: Believing the car is large enough for turning — 1200 × 1400 mm is too small for the 1800 mm turning circle
Treating 'inside the car' as correct because it feels intuitive — the lobby provides the mandatory turning space

proposed.explanation: Turning happens in the lobby (1800 × 1800 mm) — the car (1200 × 1400 mm) is too small for a turning maneuver.
